mobile.composer_input.voice.setup_needed.note: Status line under the composer after the reader taps the mic on a computer with no speech-to-text configured. Transcription runs on the computer, so the fix is there, not on the phone. Keep it short: it must fit two lines beside nothing at 320 pt and 200 % text. Full sentence with final full stop.

mobile.composer_input.voice.mic_setup.note: Accessible name of the composer's mic when the computer has no speech-to-text configured. Screen readers only; no final full stop.

mobile.composer_input.voice.mic_setup_hi.note: Accessibility hint for the mic in its not-set-up state: what a tap does (shows how to turn voice input on). No final full stop.

mobile.composer_input.voice.discard.note: Accessible name of the ✕ in the recording row: throws the recording away and sends nothing. Distinct from finishing. No final full stop.

mobile.composer_input.voice.finish.note: Accessible name of the ✓ in the recording row: stops recording and transcribes it into the draft. No final full stop.

mobile.composer_input.paste.image.note: Visible label of a small chip in the composer that appears when the clipboard holds an image; tapping attaches it. Keep short (two words). No final full stop.

mobile.composer_input.paste.image_hint.note: Accessibility hint for the Paste image chip. No final full stop.

mobile.composer_input.paste.denied.note: Error line under the composer (iOS only) after the reader pressed the Paste image chip and the system paste prompt was declined (Don't Allow). Says paste was not allowed and that pressing the same paste button again shows the system prompt again, then names the system's Allow Paste button. The quoted button name MUST match the label iOS itself shows on its paste prompt in this locale, verbatim — the reader looks for that exact word on the system dialog, so a paraphrase or a fresh translation sends them looking for a button that does not exist. Full sentences with final full stop.

mobile.composer_input.paste.empty_ios.note: Error line under the composer (iOS only) after the reader chose the Paste image ROW in the add-image sheet and no image came back. On iOS an empty clipboard and a declined system paste prompt look the same to the app, so this names both: copy an image first, and choose the system's Allow Paste button if it asks. The quoted button name MUST match the label iOS itself shows on its paste prompt in this locale, verbatim. Full sentences with final full stops.

mobile.composer_input.clear_draft.note: User-action button clears only the unsent editor, not queued messages or retained instructions with uncertain delivery. No final full stop.

mobile.composer_input.clear_draft_hint.note: Screen-reader hint for Clear draft. Explicitly distinguishes editor clearing from deleting queued or unconfirmed instructions.

mobile.composer_input.dismiss_error.note: Presentation-only error dismissal. Does not retry, delete or acknowledge delivery. The accessible name of the dismissal, and also its VISIBLE text action when the error line sits under a retained-instruction sentence, where a bare Dismiss would read as dismissing that sentence. Keep it short; no final full stop.

mobile.composer_input.dismiss_error_hint.note: Screen-reader hint for dismissing only an error message. Draft and delivery records are unchanged.

mobile.composer_input.notice_retry.note: Short text action inside the composer's failure notice, trailing the sentence saying an earlier instruction may not have been delivered. Sends that instruction again. One word where the language allows; no final full stop.

mobile.composer_input.notice_dismiss.note: Short text action trailing the error line of the composer's failure notice, shown when that error is the only sentence there. Hides the error line only; it does not retry, delete or acknowledge anything. One word where the language allows; no final full stop.

mobile.composer_input.attach.library.note: Row in the composer's add-image sheet that opens the system photo picker. Use the name the operating system gives its photo library on the platform (iOS: Photos library). No final full stop.

mobile.composer_input.attach.camera.note: Row in the composer's add-image sheet that opens the camera to take one photo, which is attached to the message. Imperative verb phrase; no final full stop.

mobile.composer_input.attach.files.note: Row in the composer's add-image sheet that opens the system document picker (the Files app on iOS), limited to images: the label says so (the relay accepts images only, so a PDF would be greyed out). Use the platform's own name for the Files app where it has one. No final full stop.

mobile.composer_input.attach.paste.note: Row in the composer's add-image sheet that attaches the image currently on the clipboard. No final full stop.

mobile.composer_input.attach.choose_imag.note: Row in the add-image sheet on the web build, where the browser's file chooser is the only image source. No final full stop.

mobile.composer_input.attach.camera_deni.note: Notice inside the add-image sheet when the reader has refused camera access for this app; the only way back is the system Settings app, which the action beside it opens. Must not blame the reader. Two short sentences with final full stops.

mobile.composer_input.attach.camera_refu.note: Notice inside the add-image sheet when the reader has just declined the system camera prompt but the system will ask again on the next tap (Android after a first refusal). States that camera access was not allowed, then that tapping Take Photo (the row's own label, mobile.composer_input.attach.camera) shows the system prompt again; no Settings action. Must not blame the reader. Two short sentences with final full stops.

mobile.composer_input.attach.open_settin.note: Text action beside the camera-access notice; opens this app's page in the system Settings app. Use the platform's name for Settings. No final full stop.

mobile.composer_input.attach.camera_unav.note: Notice inside the add-image sheet when the device has no usable camera (for example a simulator). Full sentence with final full stop.

mobile.composer_input.attach.camera_erro.note: Error line under the composer when the camera could not be opened or the photo could not be read after the reader chose to take one. Full sentences with final full stops.
